note: Harness-neutral rule source for command_policy (see harness/harness-contract.md). prefix-rules are enforced by a native per-harness primitive (Claude Code permissions.ask, Codex .rules prefix_rule); content-rules match a token that can appear anywhere in the argument list and are enforced only where a pre-execution hook exists (Claude Code hooks/pre-bash-git-hygiene-check.mjs today). Every decision here is "ask", never a hard block: git-hygiene-protocol.md reserves an explicit, session-scoped user override for each of these rules, and a hard deny cannot express that carve-out.

prefix-rules.justification: Force-pushes rewrite remote history; git-hygiene-protocol.md Rule 2 forbids raw --force against protected branches and prefers --force-with-lease, which this rule deliberately excludes.
Blind wildcard staging risks pulling in .env, credentials, build artifacts, or in-progress work not meant for this commit.
Same risk as -A: stages every change under the current directory unreviewed.
Discards working-tree and index changes irreversibly.

Rewrites local history; risky when the affected commits already exist on a remote. A static rule cannot check push status, so this is a conservative blanket approximation of Rule 2's actual (published-commits-only) condition.
Rewrites the previous commit; risky when it already exists on a remote. Same conservative-blanket caveat as rebase above.
Named in the protocol's Scope section as a history-rewriting risk when applied onto a published branch. Same conservative-blanket caveat: a static rule cannot check the target branch.

content-rules.justification: Bypasses pre-commit, commit-msg, and pre-push hooks the user opted into. Can appear anywhere in the argument list (e.g. after -m "message"), so no prefix rule can catch it.
Disables signing via an inline config override instead of the flag form; same bypass as --no-gpg-sign.
Skips DCO signoff on a project that may enforce it.
Skips CI or required-status checks via a magic string embedded in the commit message rather than a command-line flag.
